- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing sharp reversals.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., 68+), especially if sentiment was neutral or bearish — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00/1.00), model overfits to recent noise — smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 periods.
- Model tends to underestimate mean-reversion zones — if price is below 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly above average; if above, slightly below.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum — if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid “too early” bottom calls.
- Model overreacts to sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00 after a dip, forecast may overshoot — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment is sustained.
